evidence_source_provenance.interpretation: Witness/source identity is meaningful provenance; repeated source metadata could be normalized behind an Evidence-side reference without deleting provenance.

generated_views.interpretation: One research-side archive and one Vite input are kept as exact generated views. Git can deduplicate identical blob content, but checkout/deployment/runtime still carry both copies before bundling.

intentional_or_semantic_repetition.reason: The reader needs an evidence-backed punctuation/conversion projection. It is not interchangeable with physical-line canonical Story.text or source Evidence.
Inline Mention/ruler/annotation-marker interaction is a Story-local projection; it preserves display spans and target IDs.
These are cross-reference IDs, not copies of the referenced payloads; they are comparatively small and preserve local traversal.
Repeated provenance is semantically meaningful, although stable source records could be referenced indirectly in a later runtime representation.

runtime_projection_dedup_upper_bound.interpretation: Upper bound if repeated display maps become shared/indexed runtime data. It is not a D1.0 deletion estimate and does not remove canonical source/evidence data.

story_reading_evidence_display.interpretation: The current builder passes the complete global Evidence list to each reading projection. This is display duplication, not independent source evidence.

git_and_runtime_observations.git_note: The two identical files point to one identical Git blob when Git object deduplication applies, but each generated update creates a large changed artifact/diff surface and both copies remain in checkout/deployment inputs.
git_and_runtime_observations.initial_parse_behavior: The JSON module is included in the initial Vite JavaScript asset; loadSiteBundle then calls parseSiteBundle on the complete imported object. No runtime JSON fetch or lazy shard boundary exists.

evidence_person_sketch_scene.notes: Repeated source/witness metadata; some repetition is intentional provenance, but it is a candidate shared table in D1.1.

era_cards.current_frontend_use: Story orientation, Era panel, and Story↔Era navigation use Era Cards.

eras.current_frontend_use: Required by parseSiteBundle shape checks; current reader does not directly read data.eras.

evidence.current_frontend_use: Collapsed Story/Person/Relation/Scene evidence panels read it after navigation; currently parsed at startup.

generated_from.current_frontend_use: Build provenance; not read by the reader.

historical_events.current_frontend_use: Era/event panels resolve event IDs through this array.

mentions.current_frontend_use: Story inline resolution and Person route context use mentions.

people.current_frontend_use: Person lookup, Person panel, random Person, and relation traversal use the registry.

person_sketches.current_frontend_use: Person panel and Person Explorer read sketches for the focused Person.

relations.current_frontend_use: Relation rows, ego map, and relation-context navigation use reviewed Relations.

ruler_identities.current_frontend_use: Validated for ruler Mention integrity; current reader uses projected era-card data.

ruler_mentions.current_frontend_use: Validated against projected ruler segments; current reader does not directly query the registry.

scene_contexts.current_frontend_use: Scene card is Story-local and only rendered when a record exists; it is currently loaded globally.

schema.current_frontend_use: parseSiteBundle schema guard; no reader rendering.

sources.current_frontend_use: Current reader uses reading.source_display; it does not directly read data.sources.

stories.current_frontend_use: Initial Story, random Story, Story→Person and navigation indexes use the full published list.

story_chain.current_frontend_use: Person→Story lists use the projected chain index; it can be deferred until Person navigation.

story_era_orientations.current_frontend_use: Story-local era_orientation is rendered; this parallel list is currently parser-validated only.

ui.current_frontend_use: Small reader labels and scene labels are used throughout the current UI.
